claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons have high grain-boundary density.
As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons contain significant residual interfacial strain and disorder.
Strain-induced inhomogeneity of magnetic exchange interactions at grain boundaries and interfaces dominates the low-field magnetocaloric response.
Strain-induced inhomogeneity of magnetic exchange interactions dominates magnetic hysteresis.
The high surface-to-volume ratio of the films and nanoribbons produces pronounced interfacial strain and structural disorder.
Interfacial strain and structural disorder broaden the distribution of magnetic exchange interactions.
The broadened exchange-interaction distribution produces a broadened distribution of local magnetic transition temperatures.
The broadened transition-temperature distribution suppresses the peak magnetic entropy change.
The broadened transition-temperature distribution increases hysteresis.
Nanoscale as-deposited samples have a lower peak entropy change and greater hysteresis than bulk forms.
A 250 degrees Celsius, one-hour vacuum anneal will partially relax interfacial strain while preserving nanoscale dimensions and structural integrity.
Annealing-induced strain relaxation will narrow the distribution of local magnetic transition temperatures.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will exhibit a sharper and higher peak magnetic entropy change.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will exhibit reduced magnetic hysteresis.
Magnetic hysteresis represents an energy loss relevant to a magnetocaloric refrigeration cycle.
The proposed mechanism applies below 0.5 T, near a transition between approximately 100 K and 300 K, and for films no thicker than approximately 100 nm or nanoribbons with sub-micron widths.
Interfacial effects are dominant within the stated nanoscale thickness and width limits.
Excessive grain growth during annealing could worsen magnetocaloric performance.
